data.description:
## The defect

`tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone` fails against a real,
installed jscpd. The adapter reports `duplication["clones"] == 0` for a fixture that contains
two byte-identical files, so the assertion `result.duplication["clones"] >= 1` fails.

    assert 0 >= 1

## Why this is being filed now

This failure was one of the two used as evidence in bug a5f5 (`make worktree` provisioned its
venv from ambient python3, so worktrees ran Python 3.14 while CI tested 3.11-3.13). a5f5's
acceptance criteria required re-checking both on an in-matrix interpreter, because every prior
observation of them had been on an untested Python and nobody could say which were artifacts.

Re-checked on Python 3.12.13 as part of landing a5f5:

- `tests/unit/grounding/test_coverage_reconstruction.py::test_full_backend_account_is_present`
  -> PASSES. It was an artifact of the untested interpreter, and needs no ticket.
- `tests/unit/metrics/test_jscpd_dup_heldout.py::test_live_clone`
  -> STILL FAILS. So it is genuinely unrelated to the Python revision.

## Environment

    jscpd     5.0.14  (/opt/homebrew/bin/jscpd)
    python    3.12.13 (in-matrix)

The test is a live-tool test: it is skipped when jscpd is absent, so CI (which does not install
the Node toolchain) never runs it. It only fires for developers who have jscpd on PATH for
`rebar metrics`, which is why it has gone unattributed.

## Likely direction, not yet confirmed

jscpd 5.x is a major version ahead of whatever the adapter was written against; the most likely
cause is a changed report shape or changed default thresholds (`--min-lines` / `--min-tokens`)
so the fixture's clone falls under the detection floor. Confirm before fixing — this ticket
records the observation, not a diagnosis.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Root cause established: adapter contract vs jscpd 5.x behaviour, with evidence.
- [ ] `test_live_clone` passes against the installed jscpd, or the adapter's supported jscpd
      range is declared and the test skips outside it (loudly, naming the range) rather than
      failing.
- [ ] `rebar metrics` duplication is confirmed to report real clones on jscpd 5.x, not silently
      zero — a metric that reads 0 when it means "I cannot tell" is worse than `unavailable`.

## Provenance

Discovered from a5f5 while satisfying its "re-check on an in-matrix interpreter" criterion.
data.title: jscpd 5.x live-clone detection returns 0 clones, so test_live_clone fails against a real jscpd
